title: Making Garlic‑Infused Butter for Croissants with a Garlic Press
meta_description: Learn how to make garlic‑infused butter for croissants using a garlic press. Quick tips, step‑by‑step instructions, and the perfect tool for aromatic, buttery r
html:
Garlic‑infused butter can turn a plain croissant into a savory delight, and a good garlic press makes the process fast and consistent. Below you’ll find a straightforward recipe, useful techniques, and why the sturdy stainless‑steel Garlic Press is the ideal companion for this task.

Why a Garlic Press Is the Secret Weapon for Croissant Butter

When you press fresh garlic, you get a fine, evenly minced paste that releases more allicin—the compound that gives garlic its punch—than chopping with a knife. That means you need less garlic to achieve a bold flavor, and the butter stays silky instead of turning grainy. The Garlic Press’s stainless‑steel body and silicone grip let you squeeze through a head of garlic in seconds, then rinse clean with a quick swish of water. No lingering odor on your hands, no crushing of the bulb, just pure, fresh garlic ready for butter.

Ingredients and Tools

  • 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted, high‑fat butter, softened to room temperature
  • 3–4 fresh garlic cloves (adjust to taste)
  • 1 teaspoon fresh lemon zest (optional, brightens the flavor)
  • ½ teaspoon sea salt, or to taste
  • Pinch of freshly ground black pepper
  • Garlic Press (stainless steel & silicone model)
  • Small mixing bowl, rubber spatula, and a piece of parchment or wax paper

Step‑by‑Step: Making Garlic‑Infused Butter

1. Prep the garlic. Separate the cloves, trim the ends, and place them in the Garlic Press. Squeeze each clove once into a small dish. The press yields a smooth paste that integrates easily into butter without any fibrous bits.

2. Combine butter and garlic. Transfer the softened butter to the mixing bowl. Add the pressed garlic, sea salt, and pepper. If you’re using lemon zest, grate it directly over the bowl now. Using a rubber spatula, fold the ingredients together until the garlic is evenly distributed. The butter should stay creamy; if it starts to look gritty, add a tiny splash of melted butter to smooth it out.

3. Chill the mixture. Lay a sheet of parchment paper on a countertop, spoon the butter onto the sheet, and shape it into a log about 1½ inches in diameter. Roll the parchment around the butter, twist the ends, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Chilling firms the butter, making it easier to slice later.

4. Use it on croissants. Slice the chilled butter log into ¼‑inch rounds. Place a slice on a warm, freshly baked croissant, let it melt, and enjoy the aromatic, buttery bite. The garlic flavor infuses the croissant without overwhelming the delicate layers.

Tips for Perfect Garlic‑Infused Butter Every Time

• Don’t over‑press. One squeeze per clove is enough; pressing too hard can release excess moisture, which may make the butter slightly watery.

• Adjust intensity. Start with three cloves for a subtle kick. Add more if you love garlic, but remember the flavor intensifies as the butter sits.

• Keep butter cold. If your kitchen is warm, work in a chilled bowl or keep the butter on a cold plate while mixing. This prevents the butter from softening too much, preserving its spreadable texture.

• Flavor variations. Swap lemon zest for orange zest, or add a pinch of smoked paprika for a smoky twist. The Garlic Press still does the heavy lifting—mashing fresh aromatics quickly and cleanly.

Cleaning the Garlic Press and Maintaining Your Tool

One of the biggest hassles with kitchen gadgets is cleanup. The Garlic Press’s silicone grip is designed to release stuck garlic particles. After you’re done, simply rinse under running water, give the chamber a quick scrub with a soft brush, and shake out any remaining bits. For stubborn residue, soak the press in warm, soapy water for a few minutes, then rinse. The stainless‑steel construction resists rust, so you can let it dry on a rack and store it wherever you keep your other prep tools.

Serving Ideas Beyond Croissants

While garlic‑infused butter shines on croissants, it’s a versatile condiment. Spread it on toasted sourdough, melt it over steamed asparagus, or toss it with hot pasta for a quick, garlicky finish. The same batch can be frozen in ice‑cube trays; just pop out a cube when you need a burst of flavor.

FAQ

Can I use pre‑minced garlic instead of a garlic press?

Yes, but fresh‑pressed garlic delivers a brighter, more potent flavor and less moisture, which keeps the butter smooth. Pre‑minced garlic often contains preservatives that can alter the taste.

How long does garlic‑infused butter keep in the fridge?

Stored in an airtight container, it lasts about 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze it in portions as mentioned above.

Is the Garlic Press safe for dishwasher use?

The silicone parts are dishwasher‑safe, but to preserve the stainless‑steel finish and ensure a thorough clean, hand‑washing is recommended.
